t: Molecular Computer: Atom Count Desk — Simple
name: Molecular Computer: Atom Count Desk — Simple
title: Molecular Computer: Atom Count Desk — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] Silicon's lattice constant is 5.43 Å with 8 atoms per cell: the desk computes the atoms in any chip volume. A 1 cm³ chip holds ~5×10²² atoms — the budget that makes 'atomic-scale' concrete.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Silicon atoms per cm³ = 5.00e+22 atoms. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
chapter_source: Demonstrations of The Manifested Molecular / Atomic-Scale Computer
real_world_basis: Lattice atom counting is the real basis of nanoscale engineering.
signature_version: Signature version: the manifestation atom desk — the chapter's atomic-scale target as the budget, with the manifestation framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: the count sets the defect budget — every atom is a potential defect site.
math_note: Silicon atoms per cm³: 5.00e+22 atoms [verified]; Atoms in a 100 nm silicon cube: 5.00e+07 atoms [verified]

math_check.label: Atoms in a 100 nm silicon cube
math_check.note: corrected 2026-10-19: was '6.25e6' (unit cells, missing x8 atoms/cell); args now use 100 nm and Si a=0.543 nm

safety: No hazard; the failure mode is a design that ignores the atom count.
how_it_works: Divide the volume by the cell volume, multiply by 8 atoms per cell. The demo counts a 100 nm cube.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
Speculative = Signature-labeled, never as established fact
Every numerical claim recomputed at build time

t: Molecular Computer: DNA Logic Budget — Simple
name: Molecular Computer: DNA Logic Budget — Simple
title: Molecular Computer: DNA Logic Budget — Simple

[REAL ENGINEERING] DNA computes with strand displacement: the desk budgets the strands per gate and the reaction time per cascade. A 4-bit adder in DNA is hundreds of strands and hours — the budget says so up front.

t: Molecular Computer: Thermal Noise Floor — Simple
name: Molecular Computer: Thermal Noise Floor — Simple
title: Molecular Computer: Thermal Noise Floor — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] At atomic scale, heat is the signal's enemy: the desk computes kT per degree of freedom and the resulting error rate for a molecular switch. A switch with barrier ≫ kT is reliable; near kT it flips thermally — the floor decides.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: kT at 300 K in eV = 0.0259 eV. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
chapter_source: Demonstrations of The Manifested Molecular / Atomic-Scale Computer
real_world_basis: Thermal-noise analysis is the real basis of nanoscale reliability.
signature_version: Signature version: the manifestation noise desk — the chapter's target as the reliability target, with the manifestation framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: cool it or raise the barrier — the floor is negotiable, not ignorable.
math_note: kT at 300 K in eV: 0.0259 eV [verified]; Thermal occupancy at 1550 nm, 300 K: 3.650e-14 photons [verified]

math_check.label: Thermal occupancy at 1550 nm, 300 K
math_check.note: corrected 2026-10-19: claim was the formula text, now the computed value

safety: No hazard; the failure mode is a switch designed at the noise floor.
how_it_works: Compare the switch barrier to kT at the operating temperature; the error rate follows Boltzmann. The demo rates a room-temperature switch.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
Speculative = Signature-labeled, never as established fact
